asks: How does the team-start decision identify seats that are members of the crew, including an on-call manager seat that is busy, given the briefs name seats by a different identifier?
what: members list the `lead id`; a busy on-call manager's record id is it; the briefs name seats by id (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: At what point in a team start is a busy seat taken out of the set of launches and verdicts, relative to the name-collision check, mail retention and creating the new members?
what: a busy seat out of the launches and verdicts before the name check, `keep_mail_for` and the creates; the plan's ids unchanged (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Which live seat states count as busy for a team start, including seats waiting on the person, stalled, or limited?
what: live and not idle with nothing running: `needs-you`, `stalled?`, `limited` among them (§4.9a, §4.5a, TD-1672)

asks: How is the refusal's per-session explanation worded and built for a session that is finished, a busy one left out, or a suspended one?
what: `finished`'s `why` over the crew less busy seats, the clause beginning with the name; a finished holder named so with the team's clauses; suspended unchanged (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What does the Close offered as a cure close: only the one named session, or the whole team, and how is its safety judged?
what: a one-session Close (`ao close <id>`, the card's), `_unsafe_to_close` over the list row (§4.9a, §4.5a, TD-1672)

asks: How are a team card's live count, its stopped state and its nothing-live wording computed when busy seats are left out of the start?
what: `live`, the concluded guard and *stopped* read over the crew less busy seats; the header and §4.5a's *nothing live* reworded (§4.9a, §4.5a, TD-1672)

asks: Is a manual wind-down offered on a team whose seats wind down by themselves anyway?
what: Start and Stop now, no Wind down, since a seat winds down by itself (§4.9a, §4.5a; superseded by F15: Wind down stays)

asks: Is a seat whose name carries a suffix handled the same way as an unsuffixed seat at team start?
what: accepted at R1; reopened by F27, which adds the note

asks: Which reading of the live sessions decides who is busy for a start, and what happens when a seat turns busy after that reading or a skipped seat later closes by its own rule?
what: one `list` reading, first; a seat turning busy after refuses with its clause; a skipped seat closed by rule 3 accepted; result line and toast say what was closed and left; the confirm advisory (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What does the team card's reading expose about which seats are busy and whether a start would work, and is it available to the command line too?
what: `teamrun.rows` gains `busy` and `startable` beside `live`; `ao team list --json` carries them (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Does the busy-seat reading change the existing live count, and where is Start drawn relative to Wind down and Stop now?
what: `live` unchanged; Start drawn wherever `startable`, beside Wind down and Stop now (§4.9a, §4.5a, TD-1672)

asks: Does an idle seat holding unpushed work block a team start, or count as busy to be left running?
what: busy is any live seat a start would not close, an idle unpushed one among them (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What happens to the whole-team start versus the member-by-member replay when a start collides with something, and can a team ever be half started?
what: the whole-team start waits; the member-by-member replay runs as today; a collision is a refused create, never half a team (§4.9a)

asks: For which blocking sessions is Close offered as the cure, and what is a session that is waiting told?
what: Close only for *idle, not declared* or finished; a waiting holder told what it waits on (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Is one single reading of live sessions used for the busy decision, name check, mail retention, start moves and closing concluded seats, or can they disagree?
what: one `list` before the name check, verdicts matched by holder id, handed to `keep_mail_for`, `_start_moves`, `_close_concluded` (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What information accompanies each blocking session in a refused start, and is a single common cure line still used?
what: each holder carries `clause` and `close`, in `--json`'s `holders`, printed per holder, the one cure line gone (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: How is a standing manager seat treated when a team is started: ever busy, or refused as before?
what: never busy; refuses as today (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: How is the result of a start reported when some seats were closed and others left running, in the command output, machine output and the on-screen notice?
what: `left_running: [{name, state}]` beside `closed`, printed, `--json`, the toast (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Does the Inbox's row offering to start a team follow the same rule as the team card?
what: follows `live` unchanged (§4.9a)

asks: Does the step that closes concluded seats at start avoid closing a seat left running because busy, including in its safety check?
what: it takes the skipped ids and leaves them out of the closes, `still` and the unsafe check (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: How is a refusal clause tied to its session so that one session's name being a prefix of another's cannot confuse them?
what: the holder's name and a space (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: When a start would be allowed, is the not-concluded warning still shown, and where does the notice's per-session text come from?
what: the line not drawn where `startable`; the per-holder lines are `NamesHeld`'s text, which the toast shows (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What does the offered kill cure stop: only that one session, or the team?
what: a one-session Kill (`ao kill <id>`, or Kill on its card), never a team stop (§4.9a, §4.5a, TD-1672)

asks: Which records count as seats of the crew for this decision, and what happens to a filled extra seat?
what: over `crew()`, every record `finished` treats as a seat; a filled extra goes into `skip` only (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What does the card offer when the team definition has renamed or dropped a busy seat, so a start is impossible?
what: `startable` None where the definition renamed or dropped a busy seat; the start refuses with the Apply line (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Which page script must carry the leave-running information so the confirmation and notice can name the seats left running?
what: `data-leaves` beside `data-closes`, the confirm's leave clause and the toast's `left_running` in app.js (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Is the waiting-state reading used for a start the same strict reading the card uses, or can the card offer Start where the press would fail?
what: the start reads it strictly; `rows` sets no `startable` without one (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: When is the live-session reading taken: for every start, or only when the crew has live records?
what: only where the crew has a live record; a start of a team with none unchanged (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What is a finished seat holding unpushed work told, and is its work pushed before it is closed?
what: told it holds unpushed work, pushed before its Close (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Who works out each blocking session's explanation and cure, and what is the exception object only responsible for?
what: `_close_concluded`, from its list read and the reading, before it raises; `NamesHeld` only formats (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Does the overflow menu on a team's rollup also offer Start where it would work, and keep wind-down and stop-now?
what: `acts` gains `start` where `startable`, keeping wind-down and stop-now (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What wording describes an idle but busy seat's state (a live shell, a live subagent, unpushed work)?
what: the reading's words where idle: *idle, shell live*, *idle, subagent live*, *idle, unpushed work* (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: How is a suffixed session's refusal clause matched to the right session?
what: matched on the holder's record name, read by its `holder` id from the same list (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What cure is stated for blocking sessions that are the person's own, suspended, sat out, or held extras, and what is offered when none applies?
what: a person's session: close it yourself; suspended: today's words; sat-out or held extra: its own words; none offered Kill (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: When a team is not stopped but a start would work, which controls (Start, Wind down, Stop now) does its card draw?
what: where `startable`, Start, Wind down and Stop now all drawn whatever `g.stopped`; `start` first in the ⋯; `data-moved` as today (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: When a start is refused because of an orphan, is it refused before or after any seat is closed?
what: refused from the first reading's `orphans`, before anything is closed (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: Where is the guard that the card's live count agrees with the busy reading, and what happens where they disagree?
what: in `repo.py`, copying `startable` only where the counts agree (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: When does the start's confirmation appear and what does it say if nothing needs closing but some seats are left running?
what: `data-confirm` set wherever `leaves` is non-empty, its two wordings (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: What is shown if an extra seat turns busy in the middle of a start?
what: no holder: shown in the holders' *not concluded* tail (§4.9a)

asks: Is the usage-at-start record written for a team start that leaves live seats untouched?
what: `_mark_team_start` passes over live seat records (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: How does a start behave when a working seat from a sweep is present and the relevant switch is off?
what: today's behaviour stated: it refuses with the Apply words, accepted; the clause case holds with the switch on; nothing new to build (§4.9a, TD-1672)

asks: When does a seat close itself, and how long does a seat that comes on a question linger, in the user-facing description of the rule?
what: a seat closes once idle and pushed; an `asks` seat lingers about fifteen minutes; one with unpushed work stays until pushed and closed (the synopsis, the board item)

asks: Which seats are described as lingering after a question is answered, in the user-facing description?
what: a seat that comes on a question, the techlead or a fact-checker (the synopsis, the board item)

asks: What happens to a seat with unpushed work: does it close itself, and when?
what: stays until its work is pushed, then closes itself (the synopsis, the board item)
